subject: Urban Planning
title: Mixed-Use Zoning: Shops Below, Homes Above
description: A short lesson to help you apply Mixed-Use Zoning: Shops Below, Homes Above.

hook.text: A café on the ground floor with apartments above is the most natural urban form. Zoning made it illegal in most places.

buildup.text: Mixed-use buildings combine residential, commercial, and sometimes office space in one structure. They create walkable streets.

discovery.text: Before zoning, mixed use was the default. The butcher lived above the shop. The baker's family was upstairs.

twist.text: Separating uses was meant to protect residents from factories. Instead, it separated homes from bakeries.

climax.text: Cities are re-legalizing mixed use along transit corridors. The old neighborhood model is being rediscovered.

punchline.text: The walkable neighborhood existed. Then zoning banned it. Now we're bringing it back.

quiz.question: Why did zoning ban mixed-use buildings?
options: Mixed buildings were structurally unsafe for residential use
Separating uses was meant to protect homes from industrial pollution
Insurance companies refused to cover buildings with multiple uses
